findings: Two-class primary test completed: 73 positive and 6 negative exact transfer groups.
New-election retrospective test: 38 positive and 488 negative groups; fixed2022 models were not refitted.
2022 balanced accuracy: CP 0.896, Tucker 0.917, unfitted quota 1.000.
2026 positive-case sensitivity: CP 0.316, Tucker 0.263; most positive crossings were missed.
The simple unfitted quota reference classified both two-class tests correctly on this finite grid. This is not an exactness guarantee outside the grid.
Reserved-amount test subsets each contain only one class; zero errors there do not establish discrimination.
V1 failed the unchanged class-coverage gate before any model fit; its source, protocol and exact cells are preserved. V2 was explicitly informed by that failure.
No learned model replaces the exact allocator; no prospective blind forecast or demonstrated latency benefit is claimed.

limitations: 2026 inputs and earlier outcomes were known in development; this is a frozen retrospective challenge.
Threshold stratification uses exact 2022 labels only for partitioning; no natural-frequency or prospective sampling claim.
Known official zero-transfer baseline is an explicit model input.
Direction and district levels are categorical and must already be represented during fitting.
No rounding/clipping and no automatic production promotion; exact Rust remains authoritative.
Primary test has only six negative groups and validation only five; percentages have limited stability.
V2 label coverage was known from v1 before its protocol was frozen; the freeze precedes refitting/recomputation, not first access to these exact labels.
Scenario groups share baselines and coordinates and are not independent political events.
The quota reference uses the known represented-party vote-pool size of each election; categorical tensor fits do not encode a new year factor.
pending: Prospective blind evaluation, independent external replication and speed/user-value validation are not established.
